blocks.text: Imagine a small B2B software team that sells to operations leaders. It has a CRM and someone who can take sales calls, but nobody owns list research or reply triage. Give every bidder the same buyer roles, regions, exclusions and example of a qualified conversation. Ask which parts of the brief they would decline and why.

blocks.title: Match the operating model to the missing work
heads: Where the buyer still has work
rows: Who is assigned, who covers absences and who coaches
Assign a manager and clarify who builds lists and writes copy
Who owns research, messaging, sending and reply triage
Approve targeting, decide on ambiguous replies and take sales calls
Who calls, in what language and how dispositions are recorded
Confirm approved lists, escalation and call handoff

sections.title: Ask for proof of day-to-day ownership

blocks.text: Ask to meet the delivery lead. Have them map who approves a list, coaches a rep and covers replies when the assigned person is away. Request a redacted example of a weekly review with an actual decision and its owner. Record which tasks still require your team's time.

Use a fictional reply such as “Someone else handles this. Can you tell me what it's about?” Ask each bidder to show how it records the referral, verifies the new role, decides what to send and alerts sales. Keep the record as an open reply until there is enough evidence for a qualified handoff.

sections.title: Decide what happens at renewal or exit

blocks.text: Agree on a review date and the evidence required to continue. Request a sample export with account IDs, message versions, reply history and dispositions. Confirm who can revoke access and who retains working assets. Revisit the decision if the promised backup or triage coverage cannot be demonstrated.

blocks.title: Shortlist decision record
rows: A live handoff demonstration and a named backup role
One owner for approvals and escalations
The provider cannot show how disputed or uncertain replies are handled

answer: Shortlist an outsourced SDR provider by the job your team needs done. Give each bidder the same brief, then verify who does the work and how they handle an uncertain reply.
description: Compare outsourced SDR companies with one buyer brief. Verify staffing, supervision, qualification, CRM handoff and what you retain at the end.
